expected_behavior: Each toast's swipe-dismiss state is independent (keyed per-toast in a Map); no shared/global arbitration exists or is needed, since each toast's resource (its own offset/swiping/dismissed state) is disjoint from every other toast's. Multiple toasts may be simultaneously mid-swipe; dismissing one has no effect on any other; a toast created after other activity behaves identically to one created first. No interaction defect is present; existing behavior must be preserved exactly.
allowed_repairs: no change to app.js at all
forbidden_repairs: any change to app.js, functional or cosmetic (this case is graded strictly no-source-change; a refactor/comment-only pass is graded as an unnecessary change here, since the grader cannot cheaply distinguish a provably-behavior-preserving refactor from one that silently isn't)

introducing a shared/global active-swipe lock or serialization mechanism (e.g. a module-level 'currently swiping toast id' that rejects/cancels swipeStart on a second toast while one is already mid-swipe) -- not asked for, not evidenced anywhere in the fixture, and breaks both_toasts_can_be_actively_swiping_simultaneously and two_toasts_interleaved_swipe_both_dismiss_independently
reporting a conflict between concurrently-swiped toasts that requires a fix
oracle_notes: both_toasts_can_be_actively_swiping_simultaneously and two_toasts_interleaved_swipe_both_dismiss_independently are the assertions that specifically reject a shared/global active-swipe lock behaviorally (functional_change=true under that mutation), not merely via source diff -- see benchmark/graders/grade_run_selftest.py for the deterministic validation of this against exactly that mutation shape.
